issues.description: Constructor parameter type mismatch for class RollerCoaster: The UML in the problem statement declares the attribute 'numberOfLoopings' as type int (problem_statement.md, UML block), and the exercise instructions require constructors to accept attributes with the same types and order. In the reference solution (solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/RollerCoaster.java) the RollerCoaster constructor is declared as: public RollerCoaster(String name, char abbreviation, double numberOfLoopings) (signature at line 7), i.e. the third parameter is double. This contradicts the UML/specification which expects an int parameter for numberOfLoopings (problem_statement.md lines 26-28). The mismatch is confusing for students because the constructor parameter types must follow the UML and the exercise's constructor rules; even though Java allows widening from int to double at call sites, the declared signature does not match the specified UML type and will cause students to implement a different constructor than required.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the RollerCoaster constructor with the UML/problem statement by changing its third parameter to int. Update the constructor signature to: public RollerCoaster(String name, char abbreviation, int numberOfLoopings) and assign the parameter directly to the int field (remove any double parameter and cast). Also update any callers/ subclasses (e.g., LaunchedRollerCoaster) to match this signature if necessary (they already use int in their constructor), ensuring all constructor signatures follow the UML-specified types and the exercise constructor-order rule.
